Adding the cross-team metrics bundle (see linked Drive) — summary below.

Summary: comparing top-quartile deliverables across Platform and Core Services shows longer ramp in Platform (median time-to-impact ~9 months) vs Core (~6 months). That means a raw snapshot risks undercounting trajectory for Platform ICs. Proposal: adopt a lightweight band-smoothing rule for mid-tenure hires where trajectory (slope > threshold) is visible across two consecutive quarters. Practical rule sketch:
- If trajectory_score >= 0.6 AND manager_case_note corroborates acceleration, apply +0.5 band smoothing;
- Smoothing applies only for rating assignment, not immediate compensation adjustments (triggers a review window).

Open question: how do we record this in a way that's auditable for later appeals? I suggest a required case note template and an entry in People Ops ledger. Mina — tagging you for HR precedent here.

Vivek
VP, Engineering Operations

Thanks for the heads up — good, practical thread. A few policy notes and constraints from People Ops:

1) Audit trail: any smoothing applied must have an associated case note with explicit rationale, dates, and manager signature. We will create an entry in the People Ledger (linked) for the current calibration batch.
2) Compensation decoupling: HR prefers smoothing only for rating assignment and suggests a 3-month review checkpoint before any comp/bonus adjustments. This protects pay equity and auditability.
3) Appeals: employees must be told the rationale in writing if their band is adjusted due to smoothing; manager communications should be templated.

I've attached a short template (band-smoothing-proposal.xlsx sheet) and added comments to the agenda. Also: if we adopt a rule that references "trajectory_score", define the score algorithm in a shared doc now — we can't retro-fit later.

I'll join Friday's session and can cover the policy/appeals segment.

—Mina
